reason: SERV Prompt Guard held every pass (3). Route this report to a human reviewer.

evidence.claim: Changing the asset's slashing handler in Core's assetSlashingHandlers mapping makes NativeVault.slashAssets revert (NotSlashStore), DoSing slashing for already-deployed NativeVaults.
evidence.support_reason: NativeVault.slashAssets (L299-318) reverts unless slashingHandler == self.slashStore (L308). self.slashStore is fixed at initialize (L75) from extraData and has no setter. SlasherLib.finalizeSlashing (L134-139) passes self.assetSlashingHandlers[vault.asset()] as the handler, and Core.allowlistAssets (Core.sol L85-91 -> CoreLib.allowlistAssets L67-75) can overwrite that mapping. So after a handler change, finalizeSlashing reverts for every pre-existing NativeVault.
preconditions: MANAGER (trusted) calls Core.allowlistAssets to change the handler for Constants.DEAD_BEEF after NativeVaults are deployed
A DSS then requests and finalizes a slashing on those NativeVaults

missing_evidence.item: Reachability under allowed actors: the trigger is a MANAGER-only call to allowlistAssets (Core.sol L85-91, CoreLib.sol L67-75). The README lists MANAGER as a trusted role and the policy says vault/slashing-handler allowlisting burden falls on OWNER.
missing_evidence.why: The DoS only occurs after a trusted-role action; without establishing that this misconfiguration is in-scope (not a trusted-role exclusion), the path is not reachable by an untrusted actor.
missing_evidence.resolves_when: The report cites a contest-policy clause or invariant showing a manager-driven handler change is an in-scope attack surface, or shows a non-trusted path to the same state.

missing_evidence.item: Demonstration that the DoS is not merely a temporary misconfiguration recoverable by the trusted manager (restoring the old handler) and that it constitutes a real impact beyond a self-inflicted admin error.
missing_evidence.why: The report itself concedes restoring handler A fixes it; a reversible admin misconfiguration with no attacker gain does not clearly support a DoS severity.
missing_evidence.resolves_when: The report shows a concrete loss or permanent lock (e.g., slashing permanently blocked with no trusted recovery) or a policy clause treating this as in-scope.
